This process involves three participants: the Request Assistant, the Client, and the Shop Assistants' Team.

**Client Process:**

The process begins when a new service is requested. The client enters the store and looks for a specific service. They then take a ticket representing their turn. At this point, the process diverges based on where the ticket was taken.

If the ticket was taken via an app, the client chooses the service and then waits for a designated waiting time. After waiting, they look for the product and specific criteria, then check how many tickets are ahead before waiting for their turn. Once it's their turn, the client asks for a specific request, which sends a message to the Request Assistant.

If the ticket was taken physically at the store, the client waits for their turn directly and then asks for a specific request.

After the client collects their order (triggered by delivery from the Shop Assistants' Team), they decide whether they have a new request. If yes, they return to look for a specific service again. If no, the process ends.

**Request Assistant Process:**

This process can be triggered either at a scheduled register time or when receiving a specific request message from the client. The assistant registers the request and checks if there are enough requests to respond to customer demand. If yes, they send the order request document to the Shop Assistants' Team, and the registering is complete. If no, they continue registering additional requests.

**Shop Assistants' Team Process:**

Upon receiving an order description message (from the request document), the team prepares the order. Once preparation is complete, they deliver the order to the client, ending their process when preparation is finished.

tasks.name: Take a ticket representing their turn
Look for the product and specific criteria
Check how many tickets are ahead
Check if there are enough requests

The process begins within the HR Personnel department when a clerk starts the workflow.

First, the clerk retrieves the requirement profile, followed by retrieving the job posting. After obtaining the job posting, the clerk creates a co-signature note and then forwards this co-signature note onward.

The co-signature note is then checked by the section manager. After the section manager reviews the note, a decision is made regarding whether there are any comments. If there are comments, the process returns to the clerk, who must create a new co-signature note and repeat the forwarding and review cycle. If there are no comments from the section manager, the note proceeds to the department head for further review.

The department head then checks the note. Following this review, another decision point determines whether there are comments from the department head. If the department head has comments, the process loops back to the clerk to create a revised co-signature note, forward it again, and go through the review cycle once more. If the department head has no comments, the process concludes successfully.

The note is then checked by the section manager. After reviewing, a decision is made regarding whether there are comments. If there are comments, the process returns to the clerk, who must create a new co-signature note and repeat the forwarding and review cycle. If there are no comments from the section manager, the note proceeds to the department head for further review.

The department head then checks the note. Following this review, another decision is made about whether there are comments. If the department head has comments, the process returns to the clerk to create a revised co-signature note, continuing the cycle again. If there are no comments from the department head, the process concludes successfully.

This workflow ensures that co-signature notes undergo a thorough multi-level review process, with both the section manager and department head having the opportunity to provide feedback before final approval.

The process begins within the Accounting and Controlling department when a booking system needs to be created.

First, the booking system is started. Following this, the payment is read, and then the payment automation is started.

At this point, a check is made to determine if the payment has been made. If the payment has been made, the payment is booked, and the process concludes with the payment being marked as paid.

If the payment has not been made, a reminder is sent to the customer. After the reminder is sent, another check determines whether the payment has been made following the reminder.

If the payment is made after the reminder, the payment is booked, and the process ends with the payment being paid.

If the payment is still not made after the reminder, a written dunning procedure is initiated. Following this, the reminder notice is reviewed. 

After the review, a check is made to determine if the inspection was successful. If the inspection is not successful, the reminder notice is filled out correctly, and then the reminder notice is reviewed again.

If the inspection is successful, the reminder notice is sent, and the process concludes with the reminder notice being sent.

The process at SoKnow begins when the annual meeting is upcoming.

Management starts by sending invitations to employees. Following this, two activities occur simultaneously: management leads the annual planning meeting while employees participate in the annual planning meeting.

Once both the leading and participating in the meeting are completed, management conducts a review and discussion of the current strategy. After this review concludes, two parallel activities begin: management reformulates the strategy while employees align for the strategy.

When both the strategy reformulation and employee alignment are finished, management communicates the strategy. Following the communication, management pursues the strategy, and the process ends with the annual meeting being upcoming again, signaling the cyclical nature of this annual planning process.

The process begins when Frank's lunch break starts at Global Car Manufacturing Inc. Frank first chooses his preferred lunch option.

If Frank chooses noodles, he prepares the noodles, which triggers two parallel activities: boiling water and preparing the sauce. After boiling the water, Frank adds the noodles and then waits for them to cook for 8 minutes. Simultaneously, the sauce is prepared and needs to cook for 10 minutes. Once both the noodles have cooked and the sauce is ready, Frank mixes the noodles and sauce together. He then eats his meal, and the lunch break ends.

If Frank chooses pizza, he selects an order form and decides how to place his order. He can either order online by accessing a website or order by phone by calling the pizza delivery person. Regardless of which method he chooses, Frank then places his order, which sends a message to the Pizzeria.

At the Pizzeria, the pizza delivery person receives the incoming order and prepares the pizza. Once prepared, the pizza is delivered and then handed over to Frank. This triggers a message sending the pizza to Frank.

Back at Global Car Manufacturing Inc., after placing his order, Frank waits for the pizza to arrive. He then receives the pizza and pays for it, sending payment to the Pizzeria. After paying, Frank eats his meal, and the lunch break ends.

At the Pizzeria, after handing over the pizza, the delivery person accepts the payment from Frank, and the order is completed.

The process describes Frank's lunch break at Global Car Manufacturing Inc. and its interaction with a Pizzeria.

When Frank's lunch break begins, he first chooses his preferred lunch. Based on his choice, the process takes one of two paths.

If Frank chooses noodles, he prepares the noodles, which triggers two activities to happen simultaneously: boiling water and preparing sauce. After boiling the water, he adds the noodles and waits for them to cook for 8 minutes. Meanwhile, the sauce needs to cook for 10 minutes. Once both the noodles are cooked and the sauce is ready, Frank mixes the noodles and sauce together, then eats his meal, and his lunch break ends.

If Frank chooses pizza, he selects an order form and decides how to place his order. He can either access a website to order online or call the pizza delivery person to order by phone. Regardless of the ordering method, Frank places his order, which is sent to the Pizzeria.

At the Pizzeria, the pizza delivery person receives the incoming order and prepares the pizza. After preparation, the pizza is delivered and then handed over to Frank. When Frank receives the pizza, he pays for it, sending payment to the Pizzeria where the delivery person accepts the payment, completing the order on the Pizzeria's side. After paying, Frank eats his meal, and his lunch break ends.

The process at NewTown Health Chemist begins when a prescription is received by a patient. The patient is first asked whether the prescription is for themselves. If the prescription is not for themselves and they are unable to provide additional actual patient signature or documents, the prescription remains unfilled and the process ends.

If the prescription is for the patient themselves, they show their Medicare card and prescriptions. This information is communicated to the pharmacist, who receives and checks the script details. The pharmacist then determines whether the prescription is valid. If the prescription is not valid, it remains unfilled and the process ends.

If the prescription is valid, the pharmacy information system is used to open and review the patient profile, after which the prescription information is ready to view. The pharmacist then checks if the patient appears suspicious. If the patient seems suspicious, the pharmacist contacts the GP to ask for advice. This inquiry triggers a response from the doctor, who replies to the call or email. The advice and recommendation is then provided back to the pharmacist. Following this, the decisions are confirmed, and the prescription remains unfilled as the process ends.

If the patient does not appear suspicious, the pharmacist checks the patient's status in person, including any allergies, pregnancy status, and past history. After this status check, if the patient does not pass, alternative lower dose level medicines are offered to the patient. The pharmacist then asks if the patient agrees to the alternatives. If the patient does not agree, the prescription remains unfilled. If the patient agrees, a short memo is added.

If the patient passes the status check, the correct prescribed dosage is selected. The pharmacist then performs a prescription inventory check. If the medication is out of stock, the pharmacist informs the patient about alternatives, and the prescription remains unfilled.

If the medication is in stock, the pharmacist double checks and collects the correct drugs. The pharmacy information system then calculates the Medicare costs, waivers, and total fees. Labels with consumer medicine information are printed and attached, and this information is communicated to the patient for consultation and recommendation time. The patient then pays the prescription fees and receives their prescriptions, at which point the dispensing process ends.

The process begins at Driller when a customer initiates an order.

The customer places the order, which then triggers Jane Doe to check the feasibility of the request. During this feasibility check, if the request is determined to be not feasible, an error occurs and the process is aborted.

If the feasibility check passes, there is a decision point. If an offer is already available or this is a repeat order, the process moves forward to Silke. Otherwise, if no offer exists, Jane Doe performs a price calculation and then creates and sends an offer to the customer.

After the offer is sent, there is a waiting period. Once this waiting time elapses, a decision is made regarding the customer's response. If the offer is accepted, the process continues to Silke. If the offer is not accepted, the process ends with the customer being informed that no order confirmation will be issued.

When the process reaches Silke (either from an accepted offer or from an existing offer/repeat order scenario), an order is created. Following order creation, the order is entered into production planning. After production planning is updated, an order confirmation is sent to the customer, and the process concludes with the order confirmation having been sent.

The process at SoKnow begins when an order intake occurs in the development department.

First, the requirements are described, followed by conducting a workshop. After the workshop, a project sketch is created. Once the project sketch is complete, the development department waits to receive an appointment confirmation from the customer company. Upon receiving this confirmation, a customer conversation is conducted.

Following the customer conversation, a specification sheet is written. The information from the specification sheet is then sent to the customer company. The development department subsequently waits to receive feedback from the customer company.

After receiving the feedback, project and capacity planning is performed. Next, standard open-source products are checked, use cases are defined, and costs are calculated.

At this point, a decision is made regarding whether the solution involves new development or existing products. If existing products can be used, the knowledge management systems are adjusted accordingly. If new products are required, the product is developed instead.

Regardless of which path was taken, the process converges and product acceptance is performed, with the customer company participating in this acceptance. Following the product acceptance, customer feedback is obtained, with the customer company providing this feedback directly.

Finally, follow-up projects are identified, and the process concludes with the order being completed.

The process at SoKnow begins when existing corporate designs become outdated.

The marketing department initiates the process by conducting brainstorming to generate ideas for new designs. Once the brainstorming is complete, the designer takes over and designs a new element based on the input received.

After the new element is designed, the designer reviews the designs and subsequently creates templates based on the approved designs. These templates are then sent back to the marketing department for review.

The marketing department reviews the templates and evaluates whether they are satisfactory. If the templates are not satisfactory, the designer is asked to revisit the design phase, where they review and potentially redesign the elements before creating new templates. This cycle continues until the templates meet expectations.

If the templates are deemed satisfactory, the marketing department conducts communication with management to present the new corporate designs. Management then evaluates whether the templates are acceptable for use. If management finds the templates unsatisfactory, the process returns to the designer for further refinement of the designs and templates.

If management approves the templates, the process concludes with the organization ready to use the new corporate designs.

The process begins at ADOmoney Bank's Recruitment department when an application has been received.

First, the recruitment team reviews the application documents and pre-selects candidates. After this review, the process splits into two possible paths: either the applicant proceeds further in the selection process, or a rejection is created after preselection and sent to the applicant, ending the process with the applicant being rejected after preselection.

For candidates who pass the initial screening, their application documents are examined in detail. Following this thorough examination, a decision is made based on whether the application is for a key position. If it is for a key position, a telephone interview is conducted first, after which an appointment for a personal interview is communicated to the applicant via email. If the application is not for a key position, the appointment communication is sent directly without the telephone interview.

After the appointment is communicated, there is a decision point where either the appointment communication is repeated, or the process continues by forwarding the appointment and applicant documents to the department. The personal interview is then conducted.

Following the personal interview, the process can either proceed to voting on applicants directly, or it splits into parallel activities: scheduling an appointment with the applicant for the assessment center and planning and preparing the assessment center. Once both parallel activities are complete, the assessment center is conducted.

After the assessment center, the recruitment team votes on the applicants. Based on the voting outcome, either an acceptance is written and sent to the applicant, concluding the process with the applicant being accepted, or a rejection is drafted and sent to the applicant, ending the process with the applicant being rejected after the assessment center.

The process begins at the Company within the risk management department. Upon starting, three activities are performed simultaneously: a BKR check, a Jane Doe check, and a credibility check. The BKR check and Jane Doe check must both complete before the credibility check can proceed. Once the credibility check is performed, senior risk management confirms the credibility check results.

Based on the credibility assessment outcome, the process branches. If the assessment is rejected, administration sends a rejection letter to the client, and the process ends. If the assessment is accepted, customer contact calls the client to complement information.

After calling the client, the process checks whether the information was picked up. If it was not picked up, a one-hour waiting period occurs, after which the client is called again to complement information. If the information was picked up, a loan offer is created and subsequently sent to the client.

Following the loan offer being sent, the process waits for either the client to accept the offer or for one hour to pass. If one hour passes without receiving an accepted offer, the client is reminded, and the process loops back to await the client's response or another hour passing. If an accepted offer is received, finance proceeds with the following steps: administration sends a welcome letter, the loan application is activated, the loan activation is validated, and the initial payment is executed.

Finally, administration returns the documents to the client, and the process concludes.

This process describes the food ordering and preparation workflow between a customer and a restaurant kitchen.

The process begins in two places simultaneously. On the customer side, the customer starts by ordering food. This order is communicated to the waiter in the kitchen, who receives it and sends the order to the sous chef.

The sous chef then manages the order of cooking and passes the cooking task to the chef. The chef prepares the food and, once cooking is complete, sends the finished dish back to the sous chef for review. The sous chef checks the food to ensure quality, then calls the waiter to grab the food.

The waiter receives this notification and sends the food to the customer. This delivery is communicated to the customer, who then enjoys the food. After enjoying the meal, the customer's process comes to an end.

Meanwhile, in the kitchen, once the waiter has sent the food to the customer, the kitchen process also concludes.

The communication between the customer and kitchen occurs at two key points: when the customer places an order that the waiter receives, and when the waiter delivers the finished food back to the customer.

The process for tracking learning progress begins and takes different paths depending on whether the user is a student or a teacher.

If the user is a teacher, they activate learning progress in selected objects, after which they proceed to view the status through color marking.

If the user is a student, they click on "Learning Progress" for each object. From there, the learning progress can be determined in one of two ways: either manually set by the user, or automatically determined by the instructor. Regardless of which method is used, both paths converge and lead to viewing the status through color marking.

Once the status is displayed through color marking, the system shows one of four possible states based on the color indicator. If the marking is gray, this indicates the item has not yet been started. If the marking is yellow, it means the item is in progress. If the marking is green, the item has been fully processed. If the marking shows a red cross, this indicates the item has been failed, which applies to courses, tests, and exercises.

After any of these four status outcomes is displayed, the paths merge together and the process comes to an end.

First, the HR department sends appointment suggestions to coordinate the scheduling. Once the appointments are proposed, three activities commence simultaneously: the HR department conducts the employee interview, the HR department conducts regular inquiries, and the employee confirms the appointment.

After the employee confirms the appointment, they participate in the employee meeting. Following their participation in the meeting, the employee completes the assigned training, which concludes with the training being marked as completed.

Meanwhile, after the HR department conducts the employee interview, they assign training to the employee. Both the training assignment and the regular inquiries must be completed before the process can proceed. Once both of these parallel activities are finished, the process concludes with the employee interview being marked as conducted.

The process begins when a user comes to the library within the Loan process.

First, the user is logged in through a dedicated subprocess. After logging in, the system determines the user's request, which can either be to extend media or to borrow media.

If the user wishes to extend media, the extension is processed. Following this, a check is performed: if successful, the process ends with the media being extended; if not, the process ends with the medium being returned.

If the user wishes to borrow media, they first select a medium, and then the medium is searched in the database. After the search, a check determines whether the medium is available.

If the medium is available, the user is identified, and the process concludes with the medium being lent to the user.

If the medium is not available, a notification is sent to the library user (who is not affiliated with HTW) indicating that the medium is unavailable. The process then waits for a response from the library user. The library user can either confirm the reservation or reject it.

If the reservation is confirmed (with a message received from the library user), the reservation process is carried out, and the process ends with the medium being reserved.

If the reservation is rejected (with a message received from the library user), the rental process is aborted, and the process ends accordingly.

Throughout this process, there are communications between the Loan process and the external library user, including notifications about medium unavailability and responses regarding reservation confirmation or rejection.

The process begins when an undergraduate student initiates an application for IMIS (likely a master's program at FH-SWF).

First, the student goes to the FH-SWF website, then defines their search criteria. Following this, three activities are performed simultaneously: selecting Informatics and Digitalization as the subject area, selecting Campus Soest, and selecting Master Study Course. Once all three selections are completed, the student clicks "Find a Study Course" and then clicks "Learn more" on the IMIS banner.

After viewing the IMIS information, the student clicks on "See how to apply here" and checks the application procedure. At this point, the process branches based on whether the applicant is an EU applicant.

If the applicant is not an EU applicant (international/non-EU), they apply via Uni-Assist and send their required documents to Uni-Assist. After submitting documents, they wait 10-12 weeks to receive a decision.

If the applicant is an EU applicant, two parallel paths begin: one where they proceed as an EU applicant, and another to check if they are an FH-SWF student or graduate. As an EU applicant, they apply via the FH-SWF Online Portal and send their required documents, then contact the IMIS Office. Simultaneously, if they are an FH-SWF student/graduate, they also apply via the FH-SWF Online Portal and contact the IMIS Office. Once both paths converge, EU applicants wait 4-6 weeks to receive a decision.

Both pathways (EU and non-EU) ultimately lead to the same outcome: the receipt of an admission or rejection letter, which concludes the application process.

The process at Accentis begins when a sales enquiry request is received from the Customer.

Upon receiving the sales enquiry, a decision is made based on the customer type. If it is an outbound customer, an enquiry is created. If it is an inbound customer, a contact is created instead.

After either the enquiry or the contact is created, the price and interest are qualified and sent to the customer for approval.

The process then waits for customer approval to be received from the Customer.

Once the customer approval is received, a decision point is reached. If the price is not approved, the enquiry status is updated and the process ends with the client not approving.

If the price is approved, a quote is created. Following the quote creation, a qualified requirements analysis is performed.

After the requirements analysis is completed, the enquiry status is updated. Finally, a job is created and the process concludes with the job being successfully created.

The process at Startup TZd-03 involves three participants: the Warehousing department, a Supplier, and Sales.

The process in the Warehousing department can be initiated through multiple paths. One path begins when a bill of materials is created, followed by ordering goods from the supplier. After ordering, the process proceeds to wait for one of several possible events.

At this point, an event-based decision occurs where the process waits for either: the delivery of parts from the Supplier, a supplier inquiry from the Supplier, or a timeout if no delivery occurs within 5 working days.

If a supplier inquiry is received from the Supplier, the question is clarified with the specialist department, and then the process returns to wait for the next event.

If parts are delivered by the Supplier, the quantity and quality are checked according to business rules. Based on the result of this check, if the inspection fails, the supplier is contacted. After contacting the supplier, a decision is made whether immediate shipping is possible. If immediate shipping is possible, the process returns to wait for the next event. If immediate shipping is not possible, the process ends with an escalation due to delivery issues. If the inspection passes, the goods are stored.

If no delivery occurs within 5 working days, the supplier is contacted directly. Following this, the same decision about immediate shipping possibility is evaluated as described above.

After goods are stored, the process waits to receive an order from Sales. Once an order is received, the goods are prepared and packaged, followed by shipping and goods issue.

Additionally, when a replacement delivery is requested, this communication is sent to the Supplier, and the process then returns to wait for the next event from the supplier.

The process begins at ACME AG's Procurement department when a need arises for work equipment.

First, the stock is checked to determine availability. Based on this check, one of two paths is followed.

If the work equipment is in stock, it is retrieved from the storeroom, and the process ends with the work equipment being removed from the storeroom.

If the work equipment is not in stock, the requirements are specified and quantified, followed by placing an order. After the order is placed, the process waits for one of two possible events to occur. Either the work equipment is received from the Supplier, or a period of 5 days elapses.

If the work equipment is received from the Supplier before the 5-day period expires, the process proceeds toward completion.

However, if 5 days pass without receiving the equipment, an order is placed by e-mail to the Supplier. The process then waits for the receipt of work equipment, which arrives as a communication from the Supplier.

Regardless of whether the equipment was received after the initial order or following the e-mail reminder, both paths converge, and the process concludes with the work equipment being procured.

Throughout this process, the Supplier communicates with the Procurement department by sending the work equipment, responding either to the initial order or to the follow-up e-mail order.

First, the Consulting team analyzes workshop results. Based on this analysis, they develop new strategic opportunities. Following this, the team formulates a report containing the results and objectives. Once the report is complete, it is forwarded to Management.

Management then reads the report and evaluates whether the report is in order. If the report is in order, Management immediately forwards it. If the report is not in order, Management corrects the report and then forwards it.

After either path - whether the report was immediately forwarded or corrected and forwarded - the process converges and the Consulting team formulates the consulting service based on the finalized report.

The process concludes when the consulting service has been successfully formulated.

First, the student conducts their application. Once the application is submitted, the Department of Admission and Enrollment accepts the applications. Following this, the department provides the applicant files to the WI Selection Committee.

The WI Selection Committee then checks the applicant eligibility. After the eligibility check is complete, the process returns to the Department of Admission and Enrollment, where the admission test results are evaluated.

Based on the evaluation, the department selects and admits the applicant. The student then accepts the admission offer. Once the admission is accepted, the Department of Admission and Enrollment enrolls the students and subsequently sends the enrollment documents.

The process concludes when the application process is completed.

The process begins at SoKnow when there is a need to secure personnel development needs, handled entirely by the HR department.

First, employee data is analyzed. Following this analysis, three activities are initiated simultaneously: checking personnel capacity, determining capacity requirements, and identifying training opportunities.

Once all three of these activities are completed, an employee interview is led. After conducting the interview, three parallel activities begin: allocating training, considering training requests, and considering improvement suggestions.

When all three of these activities are finished, the results are discussed with the department head. Following this discussion, training and continuing education are organized. Finally, the competency profile is updated, and the process concludes with personnel development needs being secured.

The process begins at Hochschule Mainz when there is a need to solve problems. The Support team first receives a ticket, after which a decision is made regarding whether customer participation is necessary.

If customer participation is not necessary, the Support team proceeds to solve the problem without involving the customer. Once resolved, the problem is marked as solved, notes are created for documentation, and a confirmation that the ticket is completed is sent, concluding the process with the problems being solved.

If customer participation is necessary, the Support team contacts the customer and conducts a detailed interview on the problem. Following this, a connection is established to the client of the customer, and then Support together with the Customer work to solve the problem. After attempting to solve the problem, further information is requested from the customer. At this point, there is a decision point where either the problem-solving continues by going back to work on the problem again, or if the issue is resolved, it proceeds to mark the problem as solved. Once the problem is solved, notes are created for documentation, a confirmation that the ticket is completed is sent, and the process ends with the problems being solved.

The process at Hochschule Mainz begins when a problem needs to be solved, triggering the Support team to receive a ticket.

Upon receiving the ticket, a decision is made regarding whether participation of the customer is necessary. If customer participation is not required, the Support team proceeds to solve the problem without involving the customer. Once resolved, the problem is marked as solved.

If customer participation is necessary, the Support team contacts the customer and conducts a detailed interview about the problem. Following this interview, Support connects to the client of the customer. The problem is then worked on collaboratively between Support and the customer to solve it.

After attempting to solve the problem, further information may be requested from the customer. At this point, either the problem is successfully solved, or the process loops back to continue working on the problem with the additional information gathered.

Once the problem is resolved through either path, notes are created for documentation purposes. Finally, a confirmation that the ticket has been completed is sent, and the process concludes with the problems being solved.

The process begins when a user decides to start a WoW subscription within the wow community.

First, the online tool for creating characters sends a subscription form to the applicant. The applicant then selects a payment method.

Based on the chosen payment method, the process takes one of two paths. If the applicant chooses to pay by credit card, they enter their credit card information. Alternatively, if the applicant chooses to pay by bank account, they enter their IBAN and BIC numbers.

After providing the required payment details through either path, the applicant submits the information.

Once the information is submitted, the online tool for creating characters activates the WoW subscription, and the process concludes with the end of the WoW subscription setup.

The process begins at ACME AG when an application is received from an applicant by the HR department.

Upon receiving the application, the HR department sends an acknowledgment of receipt to the applicant. The application is then forwarded to the HR manager, who checks the applicant using business rules to evaluate their qualifications.

Based on the application status, the HR manager decides the next step. If the decision is to reject the applicant, a rejection is sent to the applicant, and the process ends with the applicant being rejected.

If the decision is to invite the applicant, the HR department sends an invitation to a job interview to the applicant. Concurrently, the HR department prepares an employment contract. Following this preparation, the interview is conducted.

After the interview, a decision is made regarding the applicant's suitability. If the applicant is not suitable, the HR department sends a rejection to the applicant, and the process ends with the applicant being rejected.

If the applicant is suitable, the HR department sends the employment contract to the applicant. The process then waits until the signed employment contract is received back from the applicant. Once the signed employment contract is received, the process concludes with the signed employment contract being available.

The process begins at the Email Account Creation Portal when an email account is needed.

First, the user logs on to the email provider website. After logging on, the user chooses a package for their email account.

At this point, a decision is made regarding whether a personal account is available. If a personal account is not available, the process ends with the private account being unavailable.

If a personal account is available, the user enters the private account welcome page. Following this, the user provides their personal information.

Next, two activities occur simultaneously: the user uploads a photo ID and enters their full names. Both of these tasks must be completed before proceeding.

Once both the photo ID has been uploaded and the full names have been entered, the personal data is confirmed. After the confirmation, a new email ID and password are generated.

The process concludes with the private email being successfully created.

The customer first chooses a pizza from the menu, then orders the pizza by phone. After placing the order, the customer waits for one of two events to occur.

If the pizza arrives, the customer proceeds to pay the delivery boy for the pizza, then eats the pizza, and the process ends with the customer's hunger being satisfied.

However, if 60 minutes pass without the pizza arriving, the customer calls the pizzeria to inquire about the order. After making the inquiry, the customer continues to wait until the pizza arrives. Once the pizza finally arrives, the customer pays the delivery boy, eats the pizza, and the process concludes with the customer's hunger being satisfied.

The process at ACME AG begins when the Human Resources Department receives an application from an applicant. Upon receiving the application, a receipt confirmation is sent back to the applicant to acknowledge that their application has been received.

The Head of Human Resources then verifies the applicant using business rules to determine the application status. Based on this verification, a decision is made whether to accept or reject the applicant.

If the decision is to reject the applicant, a rejection notification is sent to the applicant, and the process concludes with the applicant being rejected.

If the decision is to accept the applicant, the Human Resources Department invites the applicant to a job interview, and this invitation is communicated to the applicant. Concurrently, an employment agreement is prepared. The job interview is then carried out with the applicant.

Following the interview, a determination is made regarding whether the applicant is suitable for the position. If the applicant is deemed not suitable, a rejection is sent to the applicant, and the process ends with the applicant being rejected.

If the applicant is found to be suitable, the employment contract is sent to the applicant. The Human Resources Department then waits to receive the signed employment contract back from the applicant. Once the signed employment contract is received, the process concludes successfully with the signed employment contract being present.

Throughout this process, multiple communications take place between ACME AG and the applicant, including the initial application submission, receipt confirmation, job interview invitation, rejection notifications when applicable, the employment contract, and the return of the signed contract.

The process begins at the FMCG Company when sample products are requested by the Warehouse Supervisor.

The Supplier then provides sample products, after which the Warehouse Supervisor evaluates whether the samples meet the requirements.

If the samples do not meet the requirements, the Supplier adjusts the product specifications and provides new sample products for evaluation again.

If the samples meet the requirements, the Warehouse Supervisor selects the product and sends a purchase order.

The Supplier then checks stock availability. If stock is not available, the Supplier restocks the inventory first. Once stock is available (either immediately or after restocking), the Supplier sends the product.

The Warehouse Supervisor receives the product and checks whether the order and physical product match.

If they do not match, the Warehouse Supervisor requests the missing products, after which the Supplier checks stock availability again and the fulfillment process repeats.

If the order and physical product match, the Warehouse Supervisor sends payment authorization to the Department.

The Department then processes the payment and notifies the supplier, at which point the process concludes with the supplier being notified.

9.text:
The process begins at the FMCG Company when sample products are requested by the Warehouse Supervisor.

The Supplier then provides sample products, after which the Warehouse Supervisor evaluates whether the samples meet the requirements.

If the samples do not meet the requirements, the Supplier adjusts the product specifications and provides new sample products for evaluation again.

If the samples meet the requirements, the Warehouse Supervisor selects the product and sends a purchase order.

The Supplier then checks stock availability. If stock is not available, the Supplier restocks the inventory before proceeding. Once stock is available (either immediately or after restocking), the Supplier sends the product.

The Warehouse Supervisor receives the product and checks whether the delivered products match the order.

If the order and physical product do not match, the Warehouse Supervisor requests the missing products. This triggers the Supplier to check stock availability again and repeat the fulfillment process.

If the order and physical product match, the Warehouse Supervisor sends payment authorization.

The Department then processes the payment and notifies the supplier.

The process concludes when the supplier has been notified.

The process begins at DLL when a risk manager initiates the workflow.

Immediately, two parallel activities are started: a BKR check is performed and a Jane Doe check is performed, both handled by the risk manager.

Once the BKR assessment is accepted, the process waits for the Jane Doe check to complete. Similarly, when the Jane Doe assessment is accepted, both checks must be completed before proceeding. After both checks are successfully completed, the risk manager performs a credibility check.

Based on the credibility assessment outcome, the process takes different paths. If the credibility assessment is accepted, a senior risk manager confirms the credibility check. Following this confirmation, the process may branch in two directions.

If the credibility assessment is ultimately rejected, an administrator sends a rejection letter, and the process ends.

Alternatively, if further information is needed, the customer relation team calls the client to complement information. After contacting the client, there is a waiting period. If the client picks up and provides the information, the customer relation team creates a loan offer. If the client does not pick up, after one hour the process loops back to attempt contact again.

Once a loan offer is created, it is checked by customer relations and then sent to the client. After sending the loan offer, the process waits for a response. Either an accepted offer is received from the client, or after one hour passes, the client is reminded. If reminded, the process loops back to wait again for acceptance or another timeout.

When the accepted offer is received, an administrator sends a welcome letter to the client. The finance team then activates the loan application, validates the loan activation, and executes the initial payment. Finally, the administrator returns documents to the client, and the process concludes successfully.

The process begins at DLL when a Risk Manager initiates the loan application assessment.

At the start, two checks are performed simultaneously: a BKR check and a Jane Doe check are both carried out by the Risk Manager in parallel.

If the BKR assessment is accepted and the Jane Doe assessment is accepted, the results converge and the Risk Manager proceeds to perform a credibility check.

Based on the credibility assessment outcome, if it is accepted, the Senior Risk Manager confirms the credibility check. Following this confirmation, there is a decision point where the process can branch in two directions.

If the credibility assessment is rejected, the Administrator sends a rejection letter, and the process ends.

Alternatively, if the credibility assessment requires additional information, the Customer Relation team calls the client to complement the information. After the call, there is a check to see if the client picked up. If the client did not pick up, the process waits for one hour and then returns to determine whether to call the client again. If the client picked up, the Customer Relation team creates a loan offer.

Once the loan offer is created, it is checked and then sent to the client. After sending the loan offer, the process enters a waiting phase where it can proceed based on two possible events: either the accepted offer is received from the client, or one hour passes.

If one hour passes without receiving the accepted offer, the Customer Relation team reminds the client, and the process loops back to wait again for either the accepted offer or another hour to pass.

When the accepted offer is received, the Administrator sends a welcome letter to the client. The Finance department then activates the loan application, validates the loan activation, and executes the initial payment. Following the payment execution, the Administrator returns the documents to the client, and the process ends successfully.

The process begins when a customer needs to resolve a problem through customer service.

First, the customer recognizes the problem they are experiencing. Once the problem is recognized, the customer contacts customer service. After making contact, the customer describes the problem to the consultation team.

The consultation team then identifies the problem based on the customer's description. Following this, the consultation team works to find a suitable solution for the identified problem. Once a solution is found, the consultation team describes the solution to the customer.

The customer then attempts to fix the problem using the provided solution. After attempting the fix, a decision is made regarding whether the solution was found helpful.

If the solution was helpful, the customer implements the solution, and the process proceeds to completion, ending with the problem being fixed.

If the solution was not helpful, the customer requests a new solution. The consultation team then suggests further solutions to the customer. After receiving these additional suggestions, the process proceeds to completion, ending with the problem being fixed.

The process for booking an oculist check appointment begins when a patient starts the booking process.

The patient first requires an appointment, describing their problem. This request is then received by the receptionist, who verifies the available dates within a 90-day window.

If there are no available dates within this period, a rejection message is sent to the patient, and the process ends.

If there are available dates, the receptionist makes an appointment and sends the appointment time and date to the patient.

The patient then checks the appointment data and decides whether to confirm it.

If the patient does not confirm the appointment, they return to require a new appointment, restarting the booking cycle.

If the patient confirms the appointment, their personal data is sent to the receptionist. The receptionist receives this email with the patient data and registers the appointment, completing the process successfully.

The process begins in the Online lane of the Purchase pool when a customer initiates a purchase.

First, the customer selects and buys goods online. This triggers the Finance department to determine whether the price requires a credit check.

If a credit check is not required, the Finance department proceeds directly to inform the warehouse about shipping.

If a credit check is required, the Finance department requests information and then checks the creditworthiness of the customer. Based on the credit check results, if the customer is deemed unworthy, the Finance department informs the customer about the rejection, and the process ends.

If the customer is deemed worthy, the Finance department informs the warehouse about the shipping.

Once the warehouse is informed about shipping, the warehouse checks if the item is available. If the item is not available, a reorder is placed, and after reordering, the availability is checked again.

If the item is available, two activities occur simultaneously: the warehouse packs and ships the order, while the Online lane sends a purchase and shipping confirmation to the customer.

After the goods are packed and shipped by the warehouse, that branch of the process ends. Similarly, once the purchase and shipping confirmation is sent online, the process concludes for that branch as well.

The process involves four participants: a Customer, a Mediation Agency, Bank A, and Bank B.

The process begins when a customer wants a credit. The customer fills out a credit application and then sends it to the Mediation Agency. The Mediation Agency forwards the loan request to both Bank A and Bank B for evaluation.

At Bank B, upon receiving the loan request, the credit amount is checked. Bank B then evaluates whether the customer's income falls between €2,000 and €100,000. If the income does not meet this criterion, a rejection is sent back to the Mediation Agency. If the income is within the acceptable range, the interest rate is determined through a subprocess, and a credit report is then sent to the Mediation Agency.

At Bank A, upon receiving the credit inquiry, the credit amount is also checked. Bank A then evaluates whether the credit amount is greater than 20 times the customer's monthly income. If it is, a rejection is sent to the Mediation Agency. If the credit amount is acceptable, an interest rate of 20% per year is estimated, and a credit report is sent to the Mediation Agency.

The Mediation Agency consolidates the responses from both banks and communicates back to the customer. After sending the credit application, the customer waits for a response. The customer may either receive a credit proposal from the Mediation Agency or receive a rejection. Regardless of which response arrives first, once the customer receives either the credit proposal or the rejection, the credit process is completed.

The process at ACME AG begins when parts are required within a department.

At this point, a decision is made based on stock availability. If the parts are in stock, the department retrieves the parts from storage, and the process concludes with the parts being successfully retrieved.

If the parts are out of stock, the department first specifies and quantifies the requirements, then completes a purchase order. This purchase order is then passed to Central Purchasing, where it is checked.

After checking the purchase order, a determination is made whether the vendor is known. If the vendor is not known, Central Purchasing creates a new vendor in the system. Once the vendor is established (or if the vendor was already known), an order template is created from the purchase order.

The purchase order then moves to the Approver, who approves it. Following approval, Central Purchasing handles the receipt of goods.

Under normal circumstances, once the goods are received, the process ends with the parts being successfully procured.

However, if delivery problems occur during the receipt of goods, this triggers an escalation. In response, Central Purchasing adjusts the order status, and the process ends with the order being cancelled due to delivery problems.

The process at SoKnow begins when the existing website is identified as outdated.

The marketing department first analyzes the current content, after which the development department reviews the current content. Following the review, two activities are performed simultaneously: designing new content and updating existing content. Once both of these activities are completed, the process continues with two parallel streams.

In one stream, the development department permanently updates the content, which concludes with the website being up-to-date. In the other parallel stream, the marketing department evaluates the content.

Based on this evaluation, a decision is made regarding whether the evaluation is positive. If the evaluation is positive, the marketing department informs management, and the process ends with the website currently needing no improvements. If the evaluation is not positive, the process loops back to the development department, where new content is designed and existing content is updated simultaneously once again, repeating the cycle of permanent updates and evaluation until the content meets the required standards.

The PC assembly process begins at the start of the workflow.

First, the workplace is prepared with an anti-static mat, tools, and gloves. Following this preparation, the motherboard is placed on the anti-static mat.

Next, the CPU is installed in the processor, after which thermal paste is applied.

At this point, a check is made to determine if installation is possible. If installation is not possible, a task is performed and the process proceeds to the end. If installation is possible, a task is carried out, which then leads to an evaluation of multiple potential issues.

Depending on the conditions identified, one or more of the following parallel paths may be taken: if there is no power, a corrective task is performed; if there is no image displayed, another task addresses this issue; if the hard drive is not recognized, a specific task handles this problem; and if a boot loop occurs, yet another task resolves this situation.

Once all applicable corrective actions from these parallel paths are completed, they converge, and another task is performed. Following this, another check is made to determine if installation is now possible.

If installation is still not possible after the troubleshooting, the process loops back to perform additional corrective work, which again leads to the evaluation of the multiple potential issues, and the troubleshooting cycle continues.

If installation is determined to be possible, a final task is completed, and the process reaches its end.

The process at Hotel Evanstonian begins when the room service manager receives an order from a hotel guest.

Upon receiving the order, the room service manager creates and forwards an order ticket. This initiates three parallel activities: the kitchen begins to prepare meals, the waiter prepares a car and then prepares non-alcoholic beverages, and the sommelier handles alcoholic beverage requests.

For the sommelier's tasks, a decision is first made regarding whether wine is desired. If wine is desired, the sommelier fetches wine from the cellar, after which they check if other alcoholic beverages are also desired. If wine is not desired, the sommelier proceeds directly to check for other alcoholic beverage requests. If other alcoholic beverages are desired, the sommelier prepares those beverages before continuing. If no other alcoholic beverages are needed, the sommelier's portion of the process is complete.

Once all three parallel activities are finished—the meals are prepared in the kitchen, the waiter has prepared the car and non-alcoholic beverages, and the sommelier has handled any alcoholic beverage requests—the process converges and the waiter delivers the desired order to the hotel guest.

After delivering the order, the waiter waits until there are no other orders to process. Once this condition is met, the waiter debits the customer's account, and the process concludes with the customer order being completed.

The process begins at the credit institution when a message is received from the company indicating that the SEC approval process has started.

Following this trigger, two activities commence simultaneously: the preparation of a registration report and the checking against Blue-Sky laws. Both of these tasks must be completed before the process can continue.

Once both the registration report has been prepared and the Blue-Sky laws check has been completed, the process again splits into two parallel paths. On one path, the credit institution prepares the determination of the issue price, which is then followed by organizing an information event. On the other parallel path, the credit institution waits to receive a registration approval message from the company.

Both paths must complete before proceeding—meaning the information event must be organized and the registration approval must be received from the company. Once these conditions are met, the issue price is decided.

After deciding the issue price, a determination is made regarding whether the obligation really occurs. If the answer is yes, the contract is concluded, and the process ends with the stock being offered to the public. If the answer is no, the process is aborted and ends with a cancellation.

The online selling process begins when a seller displays items on the webpage within the eBay data stores platform.

Once items are displayed, the buyer purchases the item. After the purchase, the seller receives the buyer's order. The seller then sends the buyer an order purchase confirmation, followed by sending the order to the shipping company.

The shipping company gets the item and then faces a decision point regarding delivery. If the delivery is on time, the shipping company delivers the item to the customer in proper dates. eBay then tracks the order, and the process concludes with the buyer closing the order.

However, if the shipping company does not deliver the purchase, the buyer must decide what action to take. If the buyer chooses to receive money, they ask for money reimbursement. The seller then receives the buyer's decision and reimburses the money, and the process ends with the purchase not being continued.

Alternatively, if the buyer chooses to receive the item instead, they ask for reshipment of the item. This request then loops back to the seller, who receives the order again and continues the process by sending another purchase confirmation and forwarding the order to the shipping company for another delivery attempt.

The shipping company gets the item and then faces a decision point regarding delivery. If the delivery is on time, the shipping company delivers the item to the customer within the proper dates. eBay then tracks the order, and the process concludes with the buyer closing the order.

However, if the shipping company does not deliver the purchase on time, the buyer must decide what action to take. If the buyer chooses to receive money back, they ask for money reimbursement. The seller then receives the buyer's decision and reimburses the money, ending the process with the purchase not being continued.

Alternatively, if the buyer prefers to receive the item, they ask for reshipment of the item. This request loops back to the seller, who receives a new order (the reshipment request), and the process continues from there with the seller sending the purchase confirmation and forwarding the order to the shipping company again for another delivery attempt.

The process begins when the Taxi System receives a booking request from a Customer.

Once the booking request is received, a Customer Service Operator checks the data provided by the customer. After reviewing the data, a decision is made regarding whether the user sent the necessary information.

If the customer did not send the necessary data, a cancellation message is sent to the Customer, and the process ends.

If the customer did provide the necessary data, the Customer Service Operator checks for available cars. Following this check, a determination is made about whether there is any available car within the next 30 minutes.

If no car is available within 30 minutes, a cancellation message is sent to the Customer, and the process ends.

If a car is available, the Taxi System displays a list of options. The Customer Service Operator then picks the nearest car with the client. After the selection is made, the Taxi System calculates the time of arrival.

Once the arrival time is calculated, the Customer Service Operator books the taxi. Finally, a booking confirmation is sent to the Customer, concluding the process.

The process begins within the AO-Software system when the program starts.

Upon program start, the player initiates the program startup. The system then checks whether to start a tutorial. If the player chooses not to start the tutorial, the system proceeds with the standard key assignment. If the player opts for the tutorial, they are directed to the tutorial section, which then leads to a tutorial covering the features on the controller.

After either completing the tutorial or proceeding with standard key assignment, the introduction is considered completed. The system then announces the selection menu to the player, who views the announcement.

At this point, the player faces a menu selection with several options. If the player chooses to access settings, they are taken to the game settings, after which the selection menu is announced again. If the player selects "Load game," the game states are retrieved, and then the game is started. If the player chooses to continue a game, the game continues and then starts. If the player decides to start a new game, a new game begins and then the game is started. Finally, if the player selects "To the tutorial," they go through the tutorial process and subsequently the tutorial for controller features is provided.

Once the game starts, two activities occur simultaneously: background music begins playing and ambient noise is generated. After both of these are completed, the system confirms the game has been loaded, followed by a command prompt appearing. The process concludes with the game having successfully started.

The process begins at the Savings bank when an application arrives from an Applicant, who sends their application (Bewerbung) to the HR team.

Upon receiving the application, the HR team sends a receipt confirmation (Eingangsbestätigung) to the Applicant. Following this, the application is reviewed according to business rules.

After the review, a decision is made regarding whether the application is in order. If the application is not in order, it proceeds toward rejection. If the application is in order, it is forwarded to the IT department for evaluation.

The IT department manually evaluates the application and then determines whether the applicant is suitable. If the decision is to reject, the process moves toward rejection. If the decision is to invite, the applicant is invited by the HR team.

Once the applicant is invited, the HR team prepares the interview and then conducts the interview. After the interview, a decision is made about whether the applicant is good. If the applicant is not considered suitable, the process proceeds toward rejection. If the applicant is deemed good, they are put on the list.

Following this, the applicant is selected, and the process moves to the Board of Directors to obtain approval. If the hiring is not approved, an error occurs and the process moves toward rejection.

If approval is obtained, the HR team confirms the applicant and then prepares the contract according to business rules. The contract signing takes place, followed by placing the applicant in the position. The position is then occupied in the system through an automated service, and the application process is completed, ending with the applicant being hired.

Throughout the process, if a cancellation occurs or if the applicant declines, the process converges toward rejection. When rejection occurs, the HR team rejects the applicant by sending a rejection notice (Absage) to the Applicant. The application documents are then archived, and the process ends with the applicant being rejected.

Following confirmation, a contract is prepared according to business rules, and then contract signing takes place. However, if the applicant declines during this phase, the process diverts toward rejection.

After successful contract signing, the applicant is placed in their position, the position is occupied in the system, and the application process is completed, ending with the applicant being hired.

Throughout the process, if rejection is warranted at any stage, the applicant is rejected and a rejection notice is sent to the Applicant. Following rejection, the application documents are archived, and the process ends with the applicant being rejected. The process begins when a customer application is recorded in the Service department.

First, the order is recorded by Service. Once the order is recorded, this information is communicated to the Finance department, where the customer data is checked.

After checking the customer data, Finance makes a decision about the order. There are two possible outcomes:

If the order is approved, Finance releases the order. This release is then communicated back to Service, where the order processing continues. The order is then printed and subsequently forwarded, concluding the process with the customer order being forwarded.

If the order is not approved, Finance rejects the order. This rejection is communicated to Service, where the customer is informed about the decision. The process then ends with the customer being informed.

The process at SoKnow begins when a new marketing campaign is upcoming.

First, management plans the focal points for the campaign. This is then handed over to the marketing department, where ideas are designed based on these focal points. Following the ideation phase, the marketing department defines specifications for the campaign materials.

Once specifications are defined, an order is sent to the external marketing agency. The marketing department then waits to receive drafts from the agency. When drafts arrive from the external agency, the marketing department evaluates the agency drafts and then votes on the drafts.

If the vote is positive, the marketing department informs management, who then evaluates the drafts. If management's evaluation is positive, they give the green light to the marketing department. The marketing department then conducts the campaign, which involves communicating with the external marketing agency, and the process ends with the marketing campaign concluded.

However, if the vote on drafts is not positive, the marketing department requests new drafts from the external marketing agency. Similarly, if management's evaluation is not positive, new drafts are also requested from the agency. In both cases, after requesting new drafts, the process loops back to wait for and receive the revised drafts from the external agency, and the evaluation cycle repeats until both the marketing department's vote and management's evaluation are positive.

The process for purchasing office supplies begins when a requirement is recorded.

First, offers are obtained from suppliers. Once the offers have been gathered, each offer is reviewed. During the review, if the offer exceeds 2000 €, the offer must be approved. If the offer does not exceed 2000 €, the offer is not approved. Regardless of whether the offer was approved or not approved, the process continues to ordering goods.

After the goods are ordered, a check is made to determine if the delivery is on time. If the delivery is on time, the final acceptance of goods takes place. At this point, the goods are sent to Goods Receipt, and an inspection of the delivery is conducted.

If the delivery is complete, it is marked as correct, and payment is initiated. The payment information is then sent to Accounting/Controlling, and the process concludes with the office supplies being successfully purchased.

If the delivery is not complete, it is marked as incorrect, and suppliers are contacted. A new delivery is then requested from the suppliers. Alternatively, if the delivery was not on time, a delivery deadline is set. In both cases—after requesting a new delivery or setting a deadline—the process loops back to check again whether the delivery is on time, and the cycle continues until the delivery is received correctly and payment can be initiated.

The process begins within a department when a planned discharge is initiated.

The doctor first sets the dismissal date. Following this, three activities occur simultaneously: the doctor determines the medical care needs, discusses the further course with the patient and relatives, and the care team determines the nursing care needs.

Once the medical care needs have been determined, the discussion with the patient and relatives has concluded, and the nursing care needs have been established, the care team defines the supply facility.

After the supply facility has been defined, two parallel paths begin: the doctor creates a doctor's letter, and a decision is made regarding whether social service is required.

If social service is required, the social service team initiates further care services. After this is completed, or if social service was not required, the care team proceeds to create the dismissal documentation.

Once both the doctor's letter has been created and the dismissal documentation is complete, the care team performs the advanced tasks for discharge.

The process concludes with the dismissal of the patient.

This process describes the interaction between Customer The Bike Zone and GBI for ordering bicycles.

**Customer The Bike Zone's Process:**

The process begins when a request is started. The customer sends a request, which triggers the acceptance and processing of the customer order. Following this, the customer orders bicycles. After ordering, the customer receives the goods and subsequently receives an invoice. The customer then settles the invoice, which concludes their process with the order being finished.

**GBI's Process:**

At GBI, a separate process begins with the "Customer Order" initiation. In the Sales department, customer master data is created, followed by changing customer data if necessary. The Sales team then accepts and processes the request, processes the offer, and copies the offer to an order which is sent to the customer. The order is then accepted and processed.

Once the order is accepted, the Material Management department checks inventory. If the product is available, the product in stock is requested. If not available, goods are procured/ordered. Either path converges, and the customer order is processed. A delivery note is created, which triggers inventory control in Material Management. Material is picked, then packed/loaded and sent to the customer.

After shipping, inventory is checked in Material Management, and the Finance department creates an invoice and sends it to the customer. Upon receiving payment, the incoming payment is processed by Finance. Finally, Sales edits and displays the document flow, completing the process.

**Communications Between Organizations:**

The customer's request is sent to GBI as an inquiry ("Anfrage"). GBI responds by sending an offer ("Angebot") back to the customer. The customer's bicycle order is transmitted as an order ("Bestellung"). GBI ships the goods ("Ware") to the customer and sends an invoice ("Rechnung"). Finally, the customer's payment ("Zahlung") is received by GBI's Finance department.

The process begins within the Request Fulfilment pool when a request is initiated at the start.

The Incident Manager first verifies the request. After verification, the order is sent for request handling. The order is then received by 1st Level Support, who proceeds to log and categorize the request.

Following categorization, a check is made to determine if the request is authorized. If the request is not authorized, the process returns to the first step where the request is verified again by the Incident Manager.

If the request is authorized, the process splits into two parallel paths. In one path, the Incident Manager and 1st Level Support jointly handle Request Monitoring and Escalation. In the other path, the Service Request Fulfilment Group along with 1st Level Support execute the Request Model.

Once both parallel activities are completed, the paths merge back together. The 1st Level Support then proceeds to close and evaluate the request.

After closure and evaluation, a decision is made regarding whether there was a problem with the request processing or the Request Record. If there was a problem, the process ends by contacting the incident manager about the problem. If there was no problem, the Incident Manager provides Request Fulfilment Support, and the process concludes with a successful end.

The process begins at SoKnow's Development department when an order intake occurs.

First, the Knowledge Management System is purchased. After the purchase, the department waits to receive adjustment requests from the Customer company. Once these adjustment requests arrive, the department makes the necessary adjustments and then sends a notification back to the Customer company informing them that the adjustments have been made.

Following this notification, a search for a test group is conducted. Once the test group is identified, tests are conducted. The process then waits for the test results to determine the next steps.

If the test results are positive, test group workshops are conducted with the identified group. After the workshops, employees are trained on the system. The department then waits to receive further adjustment requests from the Customer company.

If the test results are negative, adjustments are made to address the issues, and the testing cycle repeats by conducting tests again.

After receiving adjustment requests following employee training, the process checks if there are adjustments needed. If yes, adjustments are made. After making these adjustments, a notification is sent to the Customer company that the product is finished.

The process then evaluates whether the adjustments are satisfactory. If the adjustments are satisfactory, the Knowledge Management System is implemented, and the process concludes with the order being completed.

If the adjustments are not satisfactory, further adjustments are made, and another notification about the finished product is sent to the Customer company, repeating the satisfaction check until the adjustments meet requirements.

Throughout this process, the Customer company communicates adjustment requests to SoKnow and receives notifications about completed adjustments and the finished product.
